paragraphs: [He reported:] Rabbi Yehiel said, “Arsan [crushed wheat] is good for a sick person” — Yoma 47a.

notes.text: The frozen Hyman text has ערבן; Yoma 47a reads ערסן. Rashi identifies arsan as a wheat preparation. This is the cited ancient statement, not “a guarantor is good for a sick person.” The source-glyph discrepancy remains to be checked.

The saved named Davidson Yoma 47a paragraph explicitly spells out Rabbah bar Yonatan reporting Rabbi Yechiel and reads ערסן. This supports the reporting context supplied in brackets. The frozen body has ערבן; the digital comparison does not determine whether that difference arose in print or transcription. The inherited Rashi wheat-preparation gloss is retained without a new Rashi inspection claim.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1079) reads ערסן, arsan, where the supplied digital Hebrew reads ערבן. Yoma 47a names Rabbah bar Yonatan as the transmitter and Rabbi Yehiel as the speaker. Rashi there describes a wheat preparation. Nedarim 41b has a parallel that calls him Rav Yehiel and describes preparations of old barley. The translation above follows the Yoma passage Hyman cites.
